title: Raffy Tulfo flags expired medicines, P556M Tala warehouse delays

blocks.text: Senator Raffy Tulfo slammed the Department of Health (DOH) for wasting medicine, citing a P13 million delivery worth of supplies that remained unused.
He also flagged the slow construction of a warehouse in Caloocan City despite the half-billion spent on the project.

Before he began his presentation, Tulfo made a disclaimer that the present DOH administration, led by Secretary Edwin Mercado, was not the subject of his report, as the incidents occurred before his term. He presented a video showing the Tala hub warehouse in Caloocan City that was allegedly filled with expired medicine, with footage that was dated November 19.
Tulfo’s team allegedly uncovered 16 million syringes, which were reportedly from 2022 and were going to expire by October 2027.
The senator has previously accused the DOH of hiding or burying expired medicine.

“I obtained documents showing delivery of approximately P13 million worth of expired medicines and nutrition supplies to Tala Warehouse. But I’m not convinced that the alleged burial involved only P13 million.” Tulfo said.

Tulfo said that there were also nutrition packs being bought but allowed to expire, year after year. The senator asked if it would be better to delegate the task to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).
He added that the matter should also be investigated by the Office of the Ombudsman.
Senator JV Ejercito, the DOH’s budget sponsor, said that the agency was already coordinating with the DSWD for the nutrition packs, which were focused on the first 1,000 days of babies.

“With regards po doon sa expired medicine issue, they have consolidated offices to ensure an end-to-end procurement and supply chain/ Ito po yung ginawa nila through digitalization para ma-monitor nila yung supplies and dedicated staffing for this purpose para magkaroon ng better forecasting in procurement para hindi na po masayang itong gamit,” Ejercito said.

(With regard to the expired medicine issue, they have consolidated offices to ensure an end-to-end procurement and supply chain. They are doing it through digitalization so that they can monitor the supplies and have dedicated staffing for this purpose, so that there is better forecasting in procurement so that these supplies would not be wasted.)

Ejercito said that they have shifted to PhilHealth for the Gamot program so that the DOH does not keep procuring this way. The agency also assembled a team to probe the matter and said that they will submit an investigation report to Tulfo.

Tulfo raised other matters, such as the construction of the Tala warehouse. It received P90 million in funding for construction in the 2019 budget, and continued to receive money in 2021, 2022, and 2024. The budget allotted for the construction of the Tala warehouse amounted to P556.2 million.
Despite construction spanning seven years, Tulfo said that it was only 38% complete.
“They have a fund… meron pong budget ito na P510 million but they are in the process of re-bidding, and DOH intends to complete this by 2028,” Ejercito said.

Tulfo replied that this was too expensive for a warehouse, as taken together with what was already spent, it was more than P1 billion. Ejercito responded by saying that the DOH has already contracted a third-party quantity surveyor so that there is a new, accurate estimate for the completion of the project. —LDF, GMA News
